title: Design a class that, given an immutable integer array, answers multiple queries for the sum of elements between indices i and j inclusive. The constructor may preprocess, and each query must be fast.
shortTitle: Range Sum Query Immutable: Build a Prefix Array
keyPoints: Build a prefix sum array in the constructor in O(n) time; answer each sumRange query in O(1) with one subtraction.
The prefix array has length n + 1 with a leading zero: prefix[k] = sum of the first k elements.
sumRange(i, j) = prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i], accounting for inclusive bounds and the leading-zero offset.
The design trades O(n) constructor time for O(1) per query, which is the right amortization for query-heavy workloads.
The class should be immutable: prefix array is private and final, no mutators exposed.
Use long for prefix values to avoid int overflow on large cumulative financial totals.
If updates were needed, switch to a Fenwick tree or segment tree for O(log n) update and query.

s1_definition.oneliner: Preprocess running totals in the constructor, answer each sumRange with one subtraction.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Range Sum Query Immutable** – a class design problem solved with a prefix sum array.
- **Constructor** – builds the cumulative-sum array in O(n): `prefix[i+1] = prefix[i] + nums[i]`.
- **sumRange(i, j)** – returns `prefix[j+1] - prefix[i]` in O(1).
- **Amortization** – O(n) once in the constructor so possibly millions of queries are each O(1).
- **Immutability** – the prefix array is private and final; no mutators exposed.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India hands a clerk a fixed list of monthly balances that will never change, and the clerk will be asked many times for the total between two months. He prepares once by writing running totals, and every future question is answered with a single subtraction, no matter how many questions come.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Range Sum Query Immutable is a class-design problem that tests where to pay the cost. Because the array is immutable, preprocess a prefix sum array once in the constructor in O(n) time, and then every sumRange query is a single subtraction in O(1). The prefix array has a leading zero and is one longer than the input, and a query for the inclusive range from i to j returns `prefix[j+1] - prefix[i]`.

The design insight is the amortization. You deliberately pay O(n) once so that possibly millions of later queries are each O(1). The alternative, a trivial constructor and on-demand sum per query, would make every query O(n), which is wrong for a query-heavy API.

Keep the prefix array private and final so the class truly honors its immutable contract. Use long rather than int for the prefix values because cumulative financial totals can overflow a 32-bit integer. If updates were ever needed, switch to a Fenwick tree.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, an API serves daily net amounts for a closed month, and dashboards fire many requests for the total between two days. The prefix array in the service constructor serves each request with one subtraction.

Remember one sentence: Build a prefix sum array in O(n) at construction time, and answer each range sum query with a single O(1) subtraction.
